messages:
carla_support: Hey team, customer reported a sudden spike of 502/504s for hosted inference API in us-east-1 around 2026-11-02 21:02 UTC. They see 'TLS handshake timeout' and intermittent 5xx, started right after we rotated leaf certs this morning. ticket# 35421. Can SRE/netops take a look?

matt_oncall: I'm seeing the same in our synthetic monitors — big uptick from 21:01:50 to ~21:06. Connection logs show a lot of client TLS timeouts — lots of TCP established but TLS handshake doesn't complete. No large memory spikes on workers.

ben_sre: Rolling log snippet from edge-proxy-12 (tail -n 200):
```
[21:02:03] 10.4.5.67 -> edge-proxy-12: CONNECT /v1/generate 502 tls.handshake_timeout
[21:02:04] 10.4.9.88 -> edge-proxy-12: CONNECT /v1/embeddings 502 tls.handshake_timeout
[21:02:05] 10.4.3.12 -> edge-proxy-12: CONNECT /v1/chat 502 ssl_no_cert_match
```
Notably a few 'ssl_no_cert_match' entries.

dmitri_netops: Quick DNS check across regions: one of our authoritative clouds returned an old CNAME during cert rotation propagation window. I ran:
```
dig +short canonical.example-cust.redwood.ai @ns1.edge-cloud
```
Some resolvers returned a cname pointing to old-edge-2024.cdn.example, TTLs vary 30s-5m. Looks like a partial propagation race during our cert reissue where the CDN origin changed hostnames.

carla_support: Customer says their client retries aggressively and they see exponential backoff disabled, causing a retry loop and higher observed error volume. They gave a client trace showing repeated TCP conn then handshake timeout.

matt_oncall: Can we reproduce? Steps I used locally:
1) curl -v --tlsv1.2 --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:52.23.72.10 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>'
2) Watch openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai
I hit a handshake timeout once when resolver returned the old cname.

ben_sre: Hypothesis: cert rotation changed SNI hostnames (we created new origin names), some of our internal resolvers still had old records -> some edge proxies attempted TLS to the wrong backend hostname which doesn't present the new chain, leading to ssl_no_cert_match or handshake timeout. Clients then hit our gateway which fails quickly.

dmitri_netops: Evidence: tcpdump on edge-proxy-12 shows TLS ClientHello with SNI 'api.redwood.ai' but then we forward to backend old-edge-2024 which expects SNI 'old-edge-2024.internal', mismatch -> backend drops or delays handshake. excerpt:
```
21:02:04.112 ClientHello SNI: api.redwood.ai -> forwarded to 10.8.1.22 (old-edge-2024)
21:02:04.115 backend responds with tcp-reset or no response
```

carla_support: Customer asked if we have a mitigation. They are sensitive to downtime.

ben_sre: Short-term mitigations:
- Add a fallback route to keep previous origin hostname (old-edge-2024) presenting the previous cert chain until all DNS TTLs expire.
- Temporarily widen health-check tolerance so proxies won't immediately mark backends as unhealthy during cert handshake mismatch.
- Ask customers to back off aggressive retries if possible (we can offer transient 429s to encourage client-side backoff).

matt_oncall: I triggered a config that pins SNI-to-backend mapping to the previous origin for 15min while DNS caches expire. deploy-bot: roll pinned-sni-forward 1 -> please confirm.\
deploy-bot: rollout started: pinned-sni-forward v2026-11-02-2103 initiated by matt_oncall

dmitri_netops: Also flushed a subset of internal resolver caches in us-east-1 (ns-cachepool-3) and forced re-sync with authoritative.

carla_support: Customer reports errors reduced around 21:10 UTC but they still see occasional 502s. Any follow-up actions?

ben_sre: We need a postmortem action: ensure cert rotation doesn't coincide with origin hostname changes, or if it must, ensure we maintain dual-serving for at least (max upstream TTL + jitter). Action items:
- add pre-rotation check to verify DNS TTLs across our resolver fleet (< 60s is risky).
- update runbook: if cert rotation includes hostname swap, then keep old chain served for 2x TTL.

matt_oncall: For immediate next steps:
- keep pinned-sni-forward in place until end of hour
- watch synthetic monitors and customer traffic for 30m
- outreach: carla_support to update customer and offer SLA credit if they want

carla_support: I'll update the ticket and tell them we applied a temporary rollback and are monitoring. also asked them to provide client logs (s_client, curl --trace) if we see recurrence.

dmitri_netops: FYI: attached traceroute and dig outputs in the ticket. Also found one edge PoP with a misconfigured forwarder that had 5m TTL; raising a config PR to standardize TTL to 60s across resolvers.

ben_sre: Notes to include in postmortem:
- root cause: partial DNS propagation + origin hostname change during cert rotation caused SNI/backend mapping mismatch -> handshake timeouts and ssl_no_cert_match -> 502s for customer traffic.
- mitigation applied: pinned SNI mapping + cache flush + config PR to standardize TTLs + runbook update.

matt_oncall: Monitoring shows error rate back to baseline by 21:28 UTC. I'll keep a 1hr watch.

carla_support: Customer acknowledged the update and will confirm tomorrow if they still see anomalies. Closing loop when they ack. Thanks all. :tada:

deploy-bot: rollback-complete check OK, pinned-sni-forward will auto-expire at 22:03 UTC unless extended.
